mission: Second survey world confirms the pattern — multiple sites with the same markings, and the wrongness grows stronger along their route
why_now: One site is curiosity; two is a pattern. Ben can no longer dismiss this as random anomaly.
conflict: The survey route Luke designed runs exactly along the wrongness's bearing — coincidence or design? Ben doesn't know if Luke planned this.
turning_point: Desh maps the anomalous sites and the wrongness bearing together — they form a line pointing deeper into the Outer Rim toward uncharted space
opening_hook: The second world has the same markings. Different climate, different geology, same hand.
closing_hook: The bearing points to a cluster of systems that don't appear on any navigation chart Ben has ever seen. Something is out there.
emotional_trajectory: Confirmation dread -> analytical focus -> determined pursuit

stakes.personal: Ben's growing certainty that this is bigger than a survey mission
stakes.interpersonal: Desh is reading Ben's tension — the professional friendship being tested by an unknown scope
stakes.external: The pattern points toward something deliberately hidden from modern records

setting: Second survey world — different biome, same era of ruins — then back aboard the Steady Returns for analysis
sensory_details: The wrongness stronger here — Force-perception parallax error beginning; vegetation patterns slightly off; Desh's navigation console showing the bearing line
notes: Thin place effects slightly stronger than first world. Desh might notice temperature inconsistencies or sounds carrying oddly — non-Force-sensitive baseline establishing.
